newsitem.title: USA: US corp junk bonds to see $3.5 bln in new supply.
newsitem.headline: US corp junk bonds to see $3.5 bln in new supply.

text.p: Drawn by favorable technical factors in the U.S. high-yield bond market, issuers are expected to sell over $3.5 billion in new junk bonds this week, syndicate sources said.
This week's sizable forward calendar includes high-yield debt offerings from 13 different issuers, sources said.

TransAmerican Energy Corp, a Houston-based oil and gas holding company, is preparing a $1.53 billion two-part offering, which is expected to be the largest deal of the week, they noted. Jefferies & Co Inc, a Los Angeles-based investment bank, will be the sole underwriter.

The 144A private placement will consist of $425 million principal amount of senior secured notes due 02 and $1.105 million principal amount of senior secured discount notes due 02, TransAmerican stated in a release several weeks ago.
The investment-grade bond forward calendar appears fairly light for this week, syndicate officials said.
On deck for early in the week is Branch Banking and Trust's offering of $250 million in 10-year subordinated debt, rated A3/BBB-plus via Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Also, Danish bank, Dendanske, plans to sell $500 million in 13-year subordinated step-up debt, non-callable for 10-years.
The fixed-interest rate coupon on the subordinated debt, steps-up to higher level and becomes floating rate if the security is not called within 10 years, market sources said.
Market sources said the structure is typical for Danish banks.
Merrill Lynch & Co is underwriting the deal which has been rated A2/A-minus, sources said. Merrill Lynch officials declined to comment.
Elsewhere, SunTrust Banks will launch a $250 million competitive bid offering of capital securities later on Monday, market players said.
Returning to junk bonds, syndicate officials expressed optimism that investors would be able to absorb the large amount of new supply without triggering a significant weakening in the overall market.
They pointed out that many junk bond mutual fund portfolio managers have high levels of cash on hand that they will likely invest in new offerings.

But several traders said the outlook was more uncertain. They noted secondary market levels were boosted by the thin new issue calendar last week, so some price weakness in junk bonds may be possible in the near future.
Market sources noted other issuers of high-yield debt this week include:

*Intercel Inc, a Georgia-based Personal Communications Service (PCS) company. Intercel is expected to sell $300 million in 144a 10-year senior notes via Morgan Stanely & Co. The bonds are prefunded for three-years.

*Falcon Building Products Inc. The company plans to sell $145 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes and $100 million in 10-year senior subordinated discount notes in a 144A private placement via Smith Barney Inc. Proceeds will be used to finance Investcorp's leveraged buyout of the midwestern building products manufacturer from Chicago investor Sam Zell, sources said.

*Viasystems Inc, a subsidiary of Viasystems Group. The company is expected to sell $300 million in 144a 10-year senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities Inc in order to finance recent acquisitions.
